subject: NexisPay - Hosted API data custody & retention Qs

Subject: Hosted API — quick Qs on residency & deletion SLA

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — NexisPay's compliance team had a few targeted questions about how Redwood handles customer data for the hosted API. We're putting together a short packet for our internal legal/security review. Can you confirm the following at a high level?

1) Primary region mapping: when a tenant selects "US" for geofencing, what cloud region(s) will customer data (requests, responses, embeddings) live in? Do you offer region-locking or we should assume multi-region failover?

2) Deletion workflow: if NexisPay issues a tenant data deletion request via the Console API, what are the exact steps performed by Redwood and the expected timeline to full physical removal from backups and snapshots?

3) Backups & snapshots: how long are snapshot backups retained by default and what is your policy for removing them after a customer deletion event?

4) Logs & audit: retention for request/trace logs (for debugging) vs. security/audit logs. Can we request a shorter retention window for request logs?

5) Key management & encryption-at-rest: do you support customer-managed keys for the hosted offering or is CMEK only available with private/dedicated?

If you can reply with a short Q&A and attach any existing one-page evidence we can include in our RFI, that would be ideal.

Best,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
Security & Privacy, NexisPay

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers; I attached a 1‑page summary (redwood-data-handling-summary-2026.pdf) and a small diagram of the tenant delete flow for reference. If you want we'll set up a short 20‑minute follow-up with Kim (product) to go into any of these in more detail.

1) Primary region mapping
- For "US" geofence we pin compute & long‑term storage to our US-West region by default (multi‑AZ within a single cloud region).
- We offer region‑pinning (tenant-level) for Hosted customers; multi‑region failover is available as an opt‑in policy that routes via a secondary US region only on capacity or outage.

2) Deletion workflow (hosted API) — high level
- Tenant deletion is a two‑step process: soft-delete + purge.
  * Soft-delete (immediate): marks tenant datasets as deleted and removes indexing/availability within minutes.
  * Purge: background job performs cryptographic unlinking and schedules removal from active storage and caches.
- Standard SLA: data is removed from active serving and caches within 24 hours; full purging from live storage surfaces typically completes within 5–7 days.

3) Backups & snapshots
- Incremental snapshots are retained for operational rollback; default retention for snapshots is 90 days.
- After a tenant purge we retain backup snapshots for an additional 60 days by default to support recovery requests and legal holds; snapshots are then eligible for secure deletion unless a contractually required hold exists.
- If NexisPay requires an accelerated purge policy (shorter window), we can discuss a tailored retention amendment for Enterprise contracts.

4) Logs & audit
- Request traces/debug logs: default retention 30 days (configurable per tenant).
- Security/audit logs (auth events, admin actions): retained 365 days for compliance investigations.
- Yes — Hosted customers can request reduced retention for request traces; reductions are implementable through the Console with a minimum of 7 days for operational support.

5) Key management & encryption
- Data at rest is encrypted by default using our managed KMS.
- We support customer-managed keys (CMEK) for Hosted under Enterprise agreements (we integrate with major cloud KMS providers). Full Bring‑Your‑Own‑Key for on‑prem/private deployments remains standard in Private offering.

Attachments included: redwood-data-handling-summary-2026.pdf (1p), tenant-delete-flow.png

Thanks Sean — that helps. A couple of follow-ups from our compliance team:

• On backups: when you say "eligible for secure deletion" after the 60‑day post‑purge window, can you confirm the mechanism (overwrite vs. crypto‑erase) and whether deletion is logged? We need an auditable trail showing snapshot removal.

• On the purge SLA: NexisPay policy requires complete removal from recoverable backups within 45 days of a deletion request unless a legal hold is placed. Is there a path to meet that 45‑day requirement?

• On logs: can you provide a way for us to have a JSON export of audit logs for the retention window (for ingestion into our SIEM)?

If you can confirm the deletion logging and whether we can get a 45‑day snapshot purge (or an enterprise amendment), we can close out the RFI.

Subject: Re: Hosted API — quick Qs on residency & deletion SLA

Elena — quick clarifications inline and final confirmation:

• Snapshot deletion mechanism & audit trail
- Mechanism: snapshots are crypto‑erased (we delete the snapshot metadata and rotate/zero the associated encryption keys) and then trigger secure deletion for the underlying objects per our cloud provider APIs. For added assurance we run a verification job that confirms object manifest removal.
- Audit trail: every deletion job writes an immutable audit event (timestamp, operator/process id, tenant id, snapshot id) to our security audit log. Those audit events are retained per our audit log retention (365 days) and are exportable as JSON via the Console or API.

• 45‑day snapshot purge request
- Standard hosted timelines (90d snapshot retention + 60d post‑purge grace) are in place for most customers because they balance disaster recovery needs vs. privacy. That said, we can contractually offer a 45‑day snapshot purge amendment for Hosted Enterprise customers. Practically we implement this as a post‑purge retention flag on the tenant which accelerates snapshot lifecycle deletion to target 45 days after the initial delete request; the process is logged and we provide a quarterly attestation of completed purges on request.

• Audit log exports
- Yes — NexisPay can request per‑tenant audit log exports in JSON (S3/secure transfer). We can automate daily exports for a defined retention window or provide ad‑hoc exports on a request.

Operational notes & risk controls
- Caching: KV/prefix caches are ephemeral and invalidated within minutes of a tenant soft‑delete; cached generations are not persisted to snapshot backups.
- Legal hold: any legal hold will suspend purge actions for the affected tenant and snapshot IDs and is recorded in the tenant metadata.
- SLA exceptions: in cross‑region failover events, some transient copies may exist longer; we document those scenarios in the security addendum.

I'll have Kim (product) and Priyom (security) prepare a short amendment draft if you want to pursue the 45‑day purge commitment and a sample audit‑export job for your SIEM ingestion.

Thanks again — happy to sync next week if useful.

Best,
Sean
